exam.title: IELTS Academic

sections.name: Reading
sections.description: 3 long texts with 40 questions. Academic texts from books, journals, magazines, newspapers.

instructions.text: Read the passage and answer questions 1-13.

stimulus.text_html:
The Development of the Printing Press

The invention of the printing press by Johannes Gutenberg in the mid-15th century is widely regarded as one of the most transformative events in human history. Before Gutenberg's innovation, books were copied by hand, a laborious process that made them expensive and rare. The printing press revolutionized the dissemination of knowledge...

[Full passage approximately 700-900 words about the history, technology, and impact of printing]

instructions.text: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

stimulus.text_html: Before the printing press, books were only available to wealthy people.

instructions.text: Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

stimulus.text_html: Gutenberg invented the printing press without any prior knowledge of similar technologies.

instructions.text: Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

stimulus.text_html: The printing press led to increased literacy rates across Europe.

instructions.text: Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

stimulus.text_html: Gutenberg's press could print 3,600 pages per day.

instructions.text: Complete the summary using words from the passage. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.

stimulus.text_html: Gutenberg's key innovation was the use of ___ type.

instructions.text: Complete the summary.

stimulus.text_html: The first major book printed was the ___.

instructions.text: Complete the summary.

stimulus.text_html: By 1500, an estimated ___ books had been printed in Europe.

instructions.text: Match each date with the correct event. Write the correct letter A-F.
Match each date with the correct event.
Match each date with the correct event.
Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

stimulus.text_html: What was the main impact of the printing press on religion?

options.text: It strengthened the Catholic Church's control

It led to the immediate decline of monasteries

instructions.text: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

options.text: It could print on both sides of paper

instructions.text: Read the passage and answer questions 14-26.

stimulus.text_html:
The Economics of Renewable Energy

The transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy sources has become one of the most significant economic shifts of the 21st century. While proponents argue that renewable energy represents a sustainable path to economic growth, critics point to the substantial costs and technical challenges involved...

[Full passage approximately 800-1000 words discussing economic arguments for and against renewable energy]

instructions.text: The passage has seven paragraphs, A-G. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter A-G.

stimulus.text_html: 14. A comparison of job creation between renewable and fossil fuel industries

instructions.text: Which paragraph contains the following information?

stimulus.text_html: 15. A mention of government subsidies for energy production

instructions.text: Which paragraph contains the following information?

stimulus.text_html: 16. Examples of countries leading in renewable energy adoption

instructions.text: Which paragraph contains the following information?

stimulus.text_html: 17. The challenge of energy storage

instructions.text: Do the following statements agree with the views/claims of the writer? Write YES, NO, or NOT GIVEN.

stimulus.text_html: Renewable energy is already cheaper than fossil fuels in all cases.

instructions.text: Write YES, NO, or NOT GIVEN.

stimulus.text_html: The transition to renewable energy will create more jobs than it eliminates.

instructions.text: Write YES, NO, or NOT GIVEN.

stimulus.text_html: Nuclear power should be classified as renewable energy.

instructions.text: Complete the sentences. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage.

instructions.text: Complete the sentences.

instructions.text: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

stimulus.text_html: What is the writer's overall view of renewable energy?

instructions.text: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

options.text: the reliability of renewable power supply

instructions.text: Read the passage and answer questions 27-40.

stimulus.text_html:
Cognitive Biases in Decision Making

Human decision-making is far from the rational process that classical economics once assumed. Decades of research in behavioral psychology have revealed that our judgments are systematically influenced by cognitive biases - mental shortcuts that often lead to predictable errors...

[Full passage approximately 900-1100 words about cognitive biases, their origins, and implications]

instructions.text: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

stimulus.text_html: What is the main point the writer makes in the first paragraph?

options.text: Human decisions are influenced by predictable biases
Psychology is more important than economics

instructions.text: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

stimulus.text_html: According to the passage, confirmation bias leads people to

options.text: seek information that supports their existing beliefs

instructions.text: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

why people are bad at mathematics

instructions.text: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

stimulus.text_html: What does the writer suggest about the availability heuristic?

options.text: It always leads to correct judgments

instructions.text: Complete the summary using words from the passage. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.

instructions.text: Complete the summary.

instructions.text: Complete the summary.

instructions.text: Match each bias with its correct description. Write the correct letter A-F.

instructions.text: Match each bias with its correct description.

stimulus.text_html: 36. Endowment effect

instructions.text: Match each bias with its correct description.

instructions.text: Write YES, NO, or NOT GIVEN.

sections.name: Writing
sections.description: 2 tasks: Task 1 (report/letter 150+ words, 20 min) and Task 2 (essay 250+ words, 40 min)

instructions.text: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words.
Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

stimulus.text_html:
The graph below shows the percentage of households with access to the internet in three European countries between 2005 and 2020.

[Graph showing internet access trends for UK, Germany, and France]

instructions.text: You should spend about 40 minutes on this task. Write at least 250 words.
Write about the following topic. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

stimulus.text_html:
Some people believe that universities should focus on providing academic knowledge, while others think they should also prepare students for employment.

Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

sections.name: Speaking
sections.description: Face-to-face interview with 3 parts: Introduction, Long turn (cue card), Discussion

instructions.text: The examiner will ask you general questions about yourself and familiar topics such as home, family, work, studies, and interests. This part lasts 4-5 minutes.
Answer the examiner's questions about yourself and familiar topics.

stimulus.text_html:
Topic: Your hometown

  • Where is your hometown?
  • What do you like most about your hometown?
  • Has your hometown changed much in recent years?
  • Would you recommend tourists to visit your hometown? Why/Why not?

instructions.text: You will be given a card with a topic and points to include. You have 1 minute to prepare and should speak for 1-2 minutes.
Describe the topic on the card. You have one minute to prepare and then speak for 1-2 minutes.

stimulus.text_html:
Describe a skill you would like to learn

You should say:

  • what the skill is
  • why you want to learn it
  • how you would learn it
  • and explain how this skill would be useful to you

instructions.text: The examiner will ask more abstract questions related to the Part 2 topic. This part lasts 4-5 minutes.
Discuss the following questions with the examiner.

stimulus.text_html:
Topic: Skills and Learning

  • Why do some people find it difficult to learn new skills as they get older?
  • Do you think traditional skills are still important in the modern world?
  • How has technology changed the way people learn new skills?
  • Should governments invest more in vocational training programs?
